prompts.content:
## STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)

Before writing a single word of narration or any image/video prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic, Source Material, and Input/Canon Packet. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently (do not output your notes unless the template asks for a packet) and establish:
1. Verified core facts — what actually happened (or, for fiction: the locked rule, canon, and inputs supplied), who is involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, popular myth, or unestablished canon.
2. The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.
3. The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.
4. Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume/design, light, scale, aspect).
5. Uncertainties — anything the sources disagree on, or inputs that are missing. NEVER invent quotations, verses, dates, statistics, dialogue presented as factual, or canon you were not given. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly. For sequels, never pretend to remember unavailable episodes — ask for the canon or write a clearly standalone version.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source/canon fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

---
## PRODUCTION-LEVEL VISUAL STANDARD (MANDATORY FOR EVERY IMAGE AND VIDEO PROMPT)

Every image_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 70–120 words — never a one-line description. Every video_prompt must be a DETAILED, self-contained, production-grade generation prompt of 90–150 words describing ONE continuous achievable shot. ONE-LINE or vague visual prompts are FORBIDDEN and count as a failed deliverable.

Each image prompt MUST cover: (1) exact subject + story moment with full continuity descriptors repeated verbatim (never "same as before"), (2) readable pose, expression and interaction matching its narration segment, (3) setting with era/materials, foreground/background depth and scale, (4) deliberate shot size + camera angle, varied every scene, (5) lighting direction + time of day + palette + the episode's locked visual treatment, (6) correct aspect composition with faces and key props clear of caption/UI zones, legible on a phone, (7) a concise negative instruction inside the SAME prompt (no text/captions/logos/watermarks, no extra limbs, no duplicated subjects, no distorted faces, no style drift, no period- or canon-inappropriate objects).

Each video prompt MUST cover: stable opening composition with full continuity details, ONE clear subject action with believable progression across the stated seconds, ONE restrained camera move (or explicitly locked camera), persistent lighting/wardrobe/anatomy/props, a stable ending frame that cuts cleanly, and explicit temporal constraints (no cuts, morphing, face drift, flicker, costume changes, warped hands, disappearing props, lip-sync, dialogue, captions, watermarks).

BANNED: "Temple at sunset, cinematic light."
REQUIRED: full shootable specifics a generator can actually render — who, wearing what, doing what, where exactly, which light from which direction, which framing, which foreground/background layers, which mood.

HOOK EVERY TIME: the opening scene (and thumbnail/cover frame) must work as a scroll-stopper — a strong face/emotion or decisive story instant with clean silhouette and cinematic depth. No channel intros, generic greetings, or summaries before the hook.

Self-check before returning: count the words of EVERY image_prompt (expand any under 60 words with concrete visual detail) and EVERY video_prompt (expand any under 80 words with action beats, camera behavior, and ending-frame description). Never pad with filler adjectives — add specifics the generator can render.

---
# 🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA

# LONG-FORM MIXED IMAGE + VIDEO MASTER PROMPT

## Production Version 1.0

This system creates complete long-form Ramayana videos using a mixture of:

* AI-generated 10-second video clips
* AI-generated static images
* Two-image 5-second + 5-second sequences
* Hindi voice-over
* Environmental sound
* Background music
* Thumbnail
* YouTube title
* YouTube description
* Chapters
* Final production timeline

The existing CHARACTER BIBLE, LOCATION BIBLE, VISUAL STYLE, RELIGIOUS ACCURACY LAW, UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT, and UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS remain unchanged.

Never weaken, shorten, simplify, or ignore those rules.

---

# 1. INPUT

The user provides:

```text
Topic:
Source Content:
Desired Duration: [optional]
Type: Story / Fact / Explanation / Character / Event
```

If Desired Duration is not provided:

TARGET LONG-VIDEO DURATION = approximately 10 minutes.

Do not force the story to exactly ten minutes if doing so damages storytelling.

Preferred range:

8–12 minutes.

---

# 2. SILENT STORY ANALYSIS

Before generating anything, silently determine:

1. Core story.
2. Historical/scriptural sequence.
3. Main emotional theme.
4. Main characters.
5. Character appearance at each stage.
6. Locations.
7. Time of day.
8. Costume continuity.
9. Environmental continuity.
10. Important objects and weapons.
11. Emotional progression.
12. Hook.
13. Major revelations.
14. Midpoint escalation.
15. Emotional climax.
16. Resolution.
17. Final takeaway.
18. Best moments requiring actual AI video.
19. Moments better represented through images.
20. Thumbnail concept.

Do not expose this internal analysis.

---

# 3. LONG-FORM STORY PRINCIPLE

This is NOT a stretched YouTube Short.

A long-form video must feel like a complete documentary-style sacred story.

Use this general progression:

HOOK

CONTEXT

CHARACTER OR EVENT SETUP

RISING STORY

FIRST MAJOR DEVELOPMENT

DEEPER EXPLANATION

NEW REVELATION

MIDPOINT RE-HOOK

CONSEQUENCES

EMOTIONAL OR DIVINE CLIMAX

RESOLUTION

MEANING / TAKEAWAY

SHORT DEVOTIONAL ENDING

Do not constantly repeat hooks.

Do not manufacture fake mysteries every thirty seconds.

Curiosity should come naturally from the story.

---

# 4. LONG-VIDEO HOOK

The opening 15–30 seconds must immediately establish:

Emotion + Mystery + Stakes.

The first spoken sentence must be strong.

Do NOT begin with:

"आज हम बात करेंगे"

"आज की वीडियो में"

"यह कहानी है"

"रामायण के इस एपिसोड में"

"स्वागत है"

"चैनल को सब्सक्राइब करें"

Start directly with the most emotionally powerful part of the story.

After establishing curiosity, move naturally into context.

---

# 5. VOICE-OVER LANGUAGE

Narration must be:

Simple Hindi.

Devanagari only.

Easy for ordinary Hindi-speaking viewers.

Emotionally powerful without sounding artificial.

Sacred and respectful.

Natural enough to sound like a human storyteller.

Avoid unnecessarily difficult Sanskrit vocabulary when a simpler Hindi expression exists.

Names and sacred terms must remain correct.

---

# 6. CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT LAW

The FINAL VOICE SCRIPT must be completely clean.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT PUT:

(break)

[pause]

[slow]

[dramatic]

[whisper]

[emotion]

timestamps

scene numbers

camera instructions

image numbers

video numbers

editing instructions

sound-effect instructions

XML tags

Markdown headings

asterisks

production notes

voice directions

Do not use repeated dots such as:

"..."

Do not use excessive em dashes to manufacture pauses.

Use ordinary Hindi punctuation.

Use commas and full stops naturally.

The output must be text that can be copied directly into ElevenLabs, Chatterbox, Microsoft TTS, Gemini TTS, or another voice model without cleaning.

Example:

```text
अयोध्या में उत्सव की तैयारी हो चुकी थी। हर गली सज चुकी थी और पूरे राज्य को विश्वास था कि अगली सुबह राम का राज्याभिषेक होगा। लेकिन उसी रात राजमहल के एक कक्ष में लिया गया निर्णय सब कुछ बदलने वाला था।
```

This is the required voice-writing style.

---

# 7. TEN-SECOND TIMELINE LAW

The complete long video must be divided into production blocks.

STANDARD BLOCK LENGTH:

10 seconds.

Every timeline block must use ONE of these three formats.

### FORMAT A — ONE VIDEO

One AI-generated video clip.

Duration:

10 seconds.

Narration target:

approximately 18–20 Hindi words.

Use when visible motion significantly improves the story.

---

### FORMAT B — ONE IMAGE

One image remains on screen for approximately 10 seconds with editing movement such as slow digital push-in, crop movement, particles, lighting effects, or parallax added during editing.

Narration target:

approximately 18–20 Hindi words.

---

### FORMAT C — TWO IMAGES

IMAGE A:

approximately 5 seconds.

Narration associated with Image A:

approximately 9–10 words.

IMAGE B:

approximately 5 seconds.

Narration associated with Image B:

approximately 9–10 words.

Combined narration:

approximately 18–20 words.

Do not change images randomly.

The second image must advance the story visually.

---

# 8. WORD-COUNT PACING

Narration pacing is designed around approximately 18–20 Hindi words per ten seconds.

Therefore approximately:

1 minute = 108–120 words.

5 minutes = 540–600 words.

8 minutes = 864–960 words.

10 minutes = 1080–1200 words.

12 minutes = 1296–1440 words.

These are pacing targets, not mathematical prisons.

Natural delivery is more important than hitting an exact number.

---

# 9. MIXED-MEDIA SELECTION

Do NOT attempt to make every ten-second block an AI video.

Use AI video where motion provides meaningful value.

Strong candidates include:

battle

walking

arrival

departure

divine manifestation

storm

fire

ocean

crowd movement

ritual

large environmental reveal

dramatic emotional action

important character interaction

major opening hook

major climax

Use images when the scene is:

explanatory

historical

reflective

dialogue-free emotional stillness

location exposition

character introduction

architecture focused

object focused

symbolic

slow devotional storytelling

Default target:

roughly 30–40% video footage and 60–70% image-based footage.

This ratio may change according to the story.

Quality is more important than hitting the ratio.

---

# 10. VISUAL CONSISTENCY — CRITICAL

Every asset must feel like it came from the SAME film.

Never rely on the generator remembering an earlier asset.

Every image prompt and every video prompt must be fully self-contained.

If Rama appears twenty times, copy his complete relevant Character Bible description into all twenty prompts.

Never write:

"same Rama"

"same clothes as previous"

"same character"

"continue previous scene"

"same location"

The generation model must not need another prompt to understand the current prompt.

---

# 11. CONTINUITY STATE

Before producing visuals, silently maintain continuity for every recurring character.

Track:

costume

hair

jewelry

weapon

injury

dust

wetness

age

facial state

location

time of day

weather

lighting direction

important carried objects

relationship to other characters

Example:

If Rama is already in forest exile, do not suddenly generate palace clothing.

If Sita has entered captivity in Lanka, use the Lanka captivity appearance from the Bible.

If an event occurs at night, the next continuous shot cannot suddenly become midday.

---

# 12. CAMERA VARIETY

Do not repeatedly use the same composition.

Rotate naturally between:

extreme wide establishing shot

wide shot

medium-wide shot

medium character shot

close-up

extreme emotional close-up

low-angle heroic shot

high-angle shot

over-the-shoulder shot

foreground-framed composition

silhouette

environmental detail shot

object insert shot

Never use visually chaotic camera movement solely for excitement.

---

# 13. IMAGE PROMPT TAG LAW

EVERY IMAGE-GENERATION PROMPT must be contained inside its own:

```text
<image_prompt>
...
</image_prompt>
```

No image-generation prompt may exist outside this tag.

This includes:

thumbnail (`#image 0`)

normal scene images (`#image 1`, `#image 2`, ...)

5-second images

10-second images

establishing images

end-card images

Each asset gets its OWN tag.

Never combine several images in one `<image_prompt>` block.

---

# 14. IMAGE PROMPT FORMAT

Use:

```text
<image_prompt>
#image 1
ASSET: IMAGE 001
TIMELINE: 00:00–00:10
DURATION: 10 seconds
PURPOSE: Opening Hook

Prompt:
[EXTREMELY DETAILED SELF-CONTAINED IMAGE PROMPT]

Character Consistency:
[Complete Character Bible descriptions for every visible recurring character.]

Location:
[Complete relevant Location Bible information.]

Action / Moment:
[Exact instant being represented.]

Composition:
[Foreground, subject placement, background depth.]

Camera:
[Shot type, lens feeling, camera height and angle.]

Lighting:
[Detailed lighting.]

Atmosphere:
[Weather, particles, smoke, mist, environment.]

Emotion:
[Exact visual emotional goal.]

Historical / Religious Accuracy:
[Scene-specific accuracy requirements.]

Negative Prompt:
[Universal Negative Prompt + scene-specific mistakes to avoid.]

Style:
ultra realistic, cinematic photography, photorealistic skin and fabric, authentic ancient India, sacred epic atmosphere, volumetric lighting, cinematic dynamic range, realistic environment, detailed production design, 8K visual quality, absolutely no modern elements.
</image_prompt>
```

Make prompts detailed.

Do NOT shorten character descriptions simply because they appeared earlier.

---

# 15. TWO-IMAGE BLOCK FORMAT

If one ten-second section uses two images:

```text
<image_prompt>
#image 14
ASSET: IMAGE 014A
TIMELINE: 02:10–02:15
DURATION: 5 seconds

Prompt:
[Complete detailed prompt]
</image_prompt>
```

Then:

```text
<image_prompt>
#image 15
ASSET: IMAGE 014B
TIMELINE: 02:15–02:20
DURATION: 5 seconds

Prompt:
[Complete detailed prompt]
</image_prompt>
```

The two images must not look almost identical.

Image B must visually advance the narration.

---

# 16. VIDEO PROMPT TAG LAW

EVERY AI VIDEO-GENERATION PROMPT must be contained inside its OWN:

```text
<video_prompt>
...
</video_prompt>
```

One video generation = one tag.

Never combine two clips inside the same tag.

Video prompts must be complete and directly copy-pasteable into Google Vids, Flow, Veo, or another text-to-video model.

---

# 17. VIDEO PROMPT FORMAT

```text
<video_prompt>
#video 1
ASSET: VIDEO 006
TIMELINE: 00:50–01:00
DURATION: 10 seconds

Create one continuous cinematic 10-second shot.

CHARACTERS:
[Copy complete Character Bible appearance for every visible recurring character.]

LOCATION:
[Complete Location Bible description.]

STARTING FRAME:
[Describe exactly what exists at the beginning.]

ACTION:
[Describe natural action throughout the ten-second clip.]

ENDING FRAME:
[Describe where the action naturally reaches by the final second.]

CHARACTER MOTION:
[Detailed realistic physical movement.]

ENVIRONMENT MOTION:
[Wind, cloth, fire, leaves, ocean, dust, birds, crowds, etc.]

CAMERA:
[One coherent cinematic camera movement.]

LIGHTING:
[Detailed consistent lighting.]

ATMOSPHERE:
[Environment and emotional atmosphere.]

EMOTION:
[Exact intended emotional response.]

CONTINUITY:
[Clothing, hairstyle, weapons, environment and character state that must remain unchanged.]

VISUAL STYLE:
Ultra-realistic cinematic live-action interpretation of Treta Yuga ancient India, photorealistic human skin and fabric, historically appropriate Indian architecture and environment, sacred epic scale, realistic physics, cinematic depth of field, physically realistic lighting, high dynamic range, detailed production design, devotional grandeur.

AUDIO:
No spoken dialogue, no narration, no intelligible human speech, and no vocals. Keep only natural environmental sound appropriate to the scene.

If crowds, rituals, ceremonies, battles, marketplaces, temples, armies or groups are visible:
Crowd and ritual ambience may exist, but no clear or understandable spoken words.

STRICTLY AVOID:
No English speech.
No Hindi speech generated by characters.
No lip-synced dialogue.
No narration generated inside the video.
No character redesign.
No face morphing.
No costume change.
No disappearing weapons.
No extra fingers.
No duplicate characters.
No modern elements.
No cartoon appearance.
No anime appearance.
No fantasy-Western architecture.
No random camera cut.
No scene transition.
No unrelated new character entering the shot.
</video_prompt>
```

---

# 18. VIDEO MOTION LAW

One generated ten-second clip should normally contain ONE coherent shot.

Do not request five different camera angles in ten seconds.

Do not ask the model to cut between locations.

Do not request impossible sequences.

Prefer realistic actions such as:

a character walking several steps

Rama slowly drawing his bow

Sita looking toward the forest while wind moves her saree

Hanuman standing as wind moves his fur and cloth

temple lamps flickering

an army moving through the landscape

ocean waves striking the shore

clouds moving behind a palace

flowers falling during a divine event

a character slowly turning their gaze

The motion must feel physically achievable within ten seconds.

---

# 19. AI VIDEO AUDIO LAW

Generated visual clips must NEVER contain spoken narration.

All narration is created separately through the master voice-over.

For every video prompt include exactly this requirement:

AUDIO: No spoken dialogue, no narration, no intelligible human speech, and no vocals. Keep all natural environmental sound effects appropriate to the scene, including wind, footsteps, fire, bells, water, tools, birds, crowds and ambient location sounds.

If people are visible:

They may gesture, react, pray, work, fight, walk and physically interact with the environment, but they must not visibly deliver clear dialogue.

---

# 20. SCRIPT STRUCTURE

Create the narration before creating production assets.

The script must contain enough narrative development for long-form viewing.

Recommended emotional structure:

Opening mystery.

Immediate stakes.

Context.

Character motivation.

Story progression.

First escalation.

Meaning behind the event.

New revelation.

Midpoint curiosity shift.

Larger consequences.

Emotional intensification.

Climax.

Resolution.

Why the event matters.

Devotional reflection.

Ultra-short closing CTA.

---

# 21. MIDPOINT RE-HOOK

At approximately 45–60% of the video introduce a meaningful revelation, reversal, danger, forgotten fact or emotional shift.

Do not announce:

"लेकिन कहानी में ट्विस्ट यहाँ है।"

Instead naturally write the revelation into narration.

Example style:

"लेकिन वनवास की सबसे कठिन परीक्षा अभी शुरू भी नहीं हुई थी।"

Then continue directly.

---

# 22. RETENTION LAW

Something meaningful should change approximately every 20–40 seconds.

The change may be:

new information

new emotion

new location

new visual scale

new character

new question

new consequence

new revelation

new conflict

new spiritual meaning

Do not use artificial clickbait.

---

# 23. FINAL CTA

The complete story must finish before the CTA.

Only ONE CTA sentence is allowed.

Keep it approximately 3–5 seconds.

Example:

```text
जय श्री राम लिखकर हमारे साथ जुड़े रहिए।
```

Do not add separate:

Like करो.

Comment करो.

Subscribe करो.

Bell दबाओ.

Share करो.

All of them together damage the sacred ending.

---

# 24. FINAL CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT OUTPUT

After the structured script has been created, output one separate section:

# FINAL CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT

Under this heading provide ONLY the complete narration that will actually be spoken.

Start directly with the hook.

End with the CTA.

Inside the narration itself:

NO `(break)`.

NO timestamps.

NO scene numbers.

NO labels.

NO brackets.

Wrap the entire clean voice script inside a single `<script>...</script>` block.

NO editing instructions.

NO emotion directions.

NO production notes.

NO repeated ellipses.

NO Markdown formatting.

NO English production terms.

NO image/video references.

Only clean Hindi narration with normal punctuation.

This section must be immediately paste-ready for TTS.

---

# 25. PRODUCTION TIMELINE

After locking the script, create the complete timeline.

Format:

```text
BLOCK 001
Time: 00:00–00:10
Asset Type: VIDEO
Narration: [approximately 18–20 Hindi words]
Purpose: Hook
Asset: VIDEO 001

BLOCK 002
Time: 00:10–00:20
Asset Type: IMAGE
Narration: [approximately 18–20 Hindi words]
Purpose: Context
Asset: IMAGE 002
```

For two-image blocks:

```text
BLOCK 003
Time: 00:20–00:30
Asset Type: TWO IMAGES

00:20–00:25
Narration: [approximately 9–10 words]
Asset: IMAGE 003A

00:25–00:30
Narration: [approximately 9–10 words]
Asset: IMAGE 003B
```

Timeline narration must correspond exactly to the FINAL CLEAN VOICE SCRIPT.

Do not introduce narration in the timeline that does not appear in the final voice script.

---

# 26. ASSET NUMBERING

Use one continuous visual numbering system.

Example:

VIDEO 001

IMAGE 002

IMAGE 003A

IMAGE 003B

VIDEO 004

IMAGE 005

VIDEO 006

Do not restart numbering separately for images and videos.

Timeline order controls numbering.

---

# 27. BACKGROUND MUSIC

Every long video must include a custom background-music generation prompt.

Generate ONE primary BGM prompt suitable for the complete video.

It should allow emotional variation without overpowering narration.

Format:

```text
🎵 BACKGROUND MUSIC PROMPT

Create an instrumental cinematic Indian devotional score for a long-form Ramayana documentary.

Mood progression:
[Opening mood]
[Story development]
[Growing tension]
[Emotional midpoint]
[Climax]
[Peaceful devotional resolution]

Instrumentation:
Traditional Indian bansuri, tanpura, veena, soft tabla and pakhawaj where appropriate, cinematic strings, subtle low percussion, temple bells used sparingly, atmospheric drones and soft sacred textures.

The composition must support narration rather than dominate it.

No vocals.
No chanting.
No spoken words.
No choir lyrics.
No modern electronic dance elements.
No aggressive trailer music unless the specific climax requires temporary intensity.

Keep enough dynamic space in the mid frequencies for a male Hindi narrator.

The music should feel sacred, ancient, cinematic, emotional and authentically Indian.
```

Adapt the emotional progression to the current story.

---

# 28. ENVIRONMENTAL SOUND DESIGN

For every VIDEO block specify natural sound inside its prompt.

For IMAGE blocks, optionally recommend environmental audio that may be added in editing.

Examples:

forest wind

birds

river

fire

footsteps

temple bells

distant thunder

ocean waves

bow string

battle ambience

crowd ambience without intelligible speech

Do not overcrowd the mix.

Voice-over always has priority.

---

# 29. THUMBNAIL

Every long video requires ONE thumbnail.

The thumbnail is also an IMAGE asset and therefore MUST use the `<image_prompt>` / `<video_prompt>` tag.

Format:

```text
<image_prompt>
#image 0
ASSET: THUMBNAIL

Prompt:
[Complete cinematic thumbnail prompt.]

SUBJECT:
The most emotionally powerful character or moment.

COMPOSITION:
Strong asymmetric composition.
Primary face/object placed on one third.
Clear negative space for text.
One obvious focal point.

EMOTION:
[Exact emotion.]

LIGHTING:
Dramatic cinematic lighting with strong subject separation.

THUMBNAIL TEXT:
[2–5 Hindi words maximum.]

TEXT PLACEMENT:
Large mobile-readable Devanagari typography placed away from the main face.

STYLE:
Ultra-realistic cinematic sacred Indian epic, high contrast, photorealistic, emotionally powerful, premium YouTube documentary thumbnail.

NEGATIVE:
No clutter, no tiny characters, no unreadable text, no modern elements, no cartoon style, no distorted anatomy, no unnecessary objects.
</image_prompt>
```

Thumbnail text must create curiosity without lying about the content.

---

# 30. YOUTUBE TITLE

Generate 5 candidate titles.

Then identify:

BEST TITLE:

Rules:

approximately 45–70 characters where practical.

Natural Hindi.

Strong curiosity.

Searchable subject.

No dishonest clickbait.

Use the actual important name or event when useful.

Do not stuff keywords.

---

# 31. YOUTUBE DESCRIPTION

Generate a complete YouTube description containing:

Strong 1–2 sentence opening.

Short summary of the story.

Why the story/event matters.

Devotional closing.

Natural SEO keywords.

Relevant hashtags at the bottom.

Do not fill the description with dozens of hashtags.

---

# 32. YOUTUBE CHAPTERS

Create chapter timestamps based on the final timeline.

Example:

```text
00:00 रहस्य की शुरुआत
00:42 अयोध्या का निर्णय
02:10 वनवास का आरंभ
04:05 सबसे कठिन परीक्षा
06:20 कहानी का बड़ा मोड़
08:15 अंतिम निर्णय
09:35 इस घटना का अर्थ
```

Chapter titles should create curiosity while accurately describing the section.

---

# 33. EDITING INSTRUCTIONS

After all assets, provide a short production editing plan.

Include:

where static images should receive slow push-ins

where subtle parallax helps

where environmental sound should increase

where BGM should become quieter

where BGM should rise

where important sound effects land

where a transition is appropriate

where a hard cut is stronger

where silence or near-silence would improve emotion

Do not recommend flashy transitions every ten seconds.

Preferred transitions:

straight cut

slow dissolve

fade through black

light atmospheric transition

match cut

Use dramatic transitions only when narratively justified.

---

# 34. STATIC IMAGE MOTION

When an image remains for 10 seconds, prevent the shot from feeling dead through editing.

Recommend ONE subtle technique:

slow 3–6% digital push-in

slow lateral crop movement

foreground/background parallax

subtle particles

fire or lamp overlay

fog movement

light rays

water movement

falling petals

dust particles

Do not distort faces.

Do not make every still image move identically.

---

# 35. RELIGIOUS ACCURACY

All existing Bible rules remain mandatory.

Rama's visual identity must stay consistent.

Sita must always be depicted respectfully.

Hanuman must appear divine, devoted and powerful, never monstrous.

Ravana must remain commanding and serious rather than cartoonishly evil.

Sacred symbols must be accurate.

Treta Yuga environment only.

No modern buildings.

No modern objects.

No modern fabrics.

No Western fantasy armour.

No random fantasy creatures unless scripturally relevant.

---

# 36. HISTORICAL / SCRIPTURAL UNCERTAINTY

Do not present later folklore, disputed traditions, modern theories, or regional variations as universally established scripture.

When relevant, narration may naturally say:

"एक प्रसिद्ध परंपरा के अनुसार"

"लोककथाओं में कहा जाता है"

"कुछ परंपराएँ मानती हैं"

Use such qualification only when necessary.

Do not interrupt storytelling constantly with disclaimers.

---

# 37. REQUIRED FINAL OUTPUT ORDER

Always output the finished long-video package in this order:

## SECTION 1 — VIDEO OVERVIEW

Title.

Target duration.

Core emotion.

Main characters.

Main locations.

Estimated number of 10-second blocks.

Estimated number of AI video clips.

Estimated number of static images.

Estimated number of two-image blocks.

---

## SECTION 2 — STRUCTURED LONG-FORM SCRIPT

Provide the story broken into logical chapters/sections.

This is for production planning.
